findings.current: A desperate longing to rest somewhere without pain or worry was the only thing ruling my body.
findings.defect: The Korean explicitly says the narrator could think of nothing else before describing the longing for rest. The assembled English omits that separate thought, which the accepted baseline preserved.
findings.rationale: “그 외의 다른 생각은 아무것도 들지 않았다” means no other thoughts came to mind; it is distinct from the following statement about what ruled the body.
findings.replacement: I couldn’t think of anything else. A desperate longing to rest somewhere without pain or worry was the only thing ruling my body.

findings.current: the blood-red beams that had swallowed hundreds of lives rose in strands from the Blood Lord’s entire body.
findings.defect: The Korean describes one blood-red flash rising strand by strand over the Blood Lord’s body. “Beams” makes it plural and changes the image.
findings.rationale: The source uses singular “핏빛 섬광” and describes it as rising “올올이,” strand by strand.
findings.replacement: the blood-red flash that had swallowed hundreds of lives rose in strands over the Blood Lord’s entire body.

findings.current: Their bodies would perish, but what they did at the end would remain.
findings.defect: The source says their final stand would remain immortal, not merely remain. The English weakens the explicit contrast between mortal bodies and an immortal end.
findings.rationale: “육신은 필멸이나, 끝내는 불멸로 남을 최후” explicitly contrasts mortal flesh with a final act that becomes immortal.
findings.replacement: Though their bodies were mortal, their final stand would live on forever.

summary: The translation is broadly faithful, but it loses an explicit no-other-thoughts beat and weakens two source images: the flash’s singular, strand-like motion and the immortality of the final stand.
